record.context_brief: Euler characteristic conjecture for compact affine manifolds
record.original_question: Conjecture: every compact affine manifold has Euler characteristic zero.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.10. A compact manifold has zero Euler characteristic number.

Assuming completeness, this was solved by B. Kostant and D. Sullivan... In 1975, M. W. Hirsch and W. P. Thurston ... proved that π_1(M) is built out of taking free products or forming finite extensions of solvable groups of polynomial growth, then χ(M)=0.

artifact.self_contained_problem: An affine manifold is a smooth manifold M equipped with a flat, torsion-free affine connection on its tangent bundle; equivalently, M admits an atlas whose transition maps are restrictions of affine transformations of R^n. Let M be a compact (closed) affine manifold. Prove or disprove: the Euler characteristic χ(M) is zero.
artifact.status_search_result: This is Chern's conjecture (1955) for affine manifolds. It is known in special cases: dimension 2 (Benzécri, Milnor), complete affine manifolds (Kostant–Sullivan), special/unimodular affine manifolds (Klingler, 2017), and certain fundamental-group classes (Hirsch–Thurston, 1975). A 2020 preprint by Feng–Zhang claimed a general proof but was found flawed and retracted; the conjecture remains open in general as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Chern's conjecture (affine geometry) - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Chern's conjecture for affinely flat manifolds was proposed by Shiing-Shen Chern in 1955... it remains an unsolved mathematical problem.

status_evidence.title: Chern's conjecture for special affine manifolds, Annals of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Klingler proves the Euler characteristic of a closed special affine manifold is zero.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Chern's conjecture on affine manifolds (retracted claim)
status_evidence.snippet: Feng–Zhang preprint claiming proof; flaw found and claim retracted.
